project_type: 100% Bun-native full-stack SPA: single Bun.serve() process serving an ElysiaJS REST API under /api/* and a React 19 + Tailwind CSS v4 + shadcn/ui (new-york) client bundled on-the-fly via Bun HTML imports. No Node.js, Vite, Webpack, or esbuild config.
build_system: Bun 1.4.2 only. Frontend is bundled by Bun's Fullstack Dev Server via HTML imports (import index.html into server.ts; pass as a route to Bun.serve routes). bun-plugin-tailwind is configured in bunfig.toml under [serve.static] so Bun.serve processes Tailwind CSS. QUIRK: bun-plugin-tailwind is a dev dependency added via `bun add -d bun-plugin-tailwind` plus `bun add tailwindcss@4`; it is referenced by string name in bunfig.toml. QUIRK: Elysia is mounted as the catch-all `fetch` handler in Bun.serve (return elysiaApp.fetch(req) for /api/* and 404 otherwise) while HTML routes live in the `routes` map — this keeps ONE server on ONE port. QUIRK: on Windows/PowerShell never use curl; use Invoke-RestMethod (JSON) and Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing (status). Never start a blocking foreground server during verification — launch bun in the background (Start-Job / Start-Process) or use a bounded timeout then stop it.
test_framework: bun test (Bun's built-in Jest-like test runner). Test files are named *.test.ts and live next to the code or under tests/. Use an in-memory or temp-file bun:sqlite DB in tests so store.sqlite at the root is not polluted.
build_command: bun install  (then type-check with: bunx tsc --noEmit)
verification_instructions: 1) `bun install` succeeds. 2) `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports no type errors. 3) `bun test` passes. 4) Boot the server bounded/background: `$p = Start-Process bun -ArgumentList 'run','src/server.ts' -PassThru` (or Start-Job), wait ~2s, then probe with Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing http://localhost:3000/ (expect 200 HTML) and Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:3000/api/books (expect seeded JSON). 5) Register via Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register -Body (JSON) -ContentType application/json; log in to capture the JWT; pass it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on cart/address/order/points/recommendation calls. 6) Exercise the full purchase flow (add cart item -> add address -> POST /api/orders with address_id + redeem_points -> GET /api/orders -> buy-again -> cancel within window succeeds -> construct an order row with placed_at older than 48h and confirm POST /api/orders/:id/cancel is REJECTED server-side). 7) Confirm a SECOND user cannot read the FIRST user's cart/orders/addresses/points (expect 403/404/empty, never another user's data). 8) ALWAYS stop the server afterward: Stop-Process -Id $p.Id (or Stop-Job/Remove-Job). Clean up any temp DB files.
snapshot_or_generated_files: store.sqlite is created at the workspace root on first server run (schema created + sample data seeded automatically). It is gitignored and must NOT be committed. No other generated/checked-in artifacts.
environment_constraints: Windows + PowerShell. Bun 1.4.2, bunx 1.4.2. Use ABSOLUTE paths rooted at c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore for all file creation/edits; never the system root. Never use curl; use Invoke-RestMethod / Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing. Never run a blocking foreground server — background or bounded, then stop it. Default port 3000 (override via PORT env). JWT secret from env JWT_SECRET with a documented dev fallback constant.
contribution_requirements: Greenfield build — NOTHING is pre-satisfied; every item must be authored. Hard constraints: NO Node.js/Vite/Webpack/esbuild; ONE Bun.serve() on ONE port; bun:sqlite only (no ORM with native Node bindings, a thin query layer is fine); real JWT auth with Bun.password hashing; strict per-user data isolation enforced server-side (never trust the client); shadcn style 'new-york', baseColor 'neutral', cssVariables true, iconLibrary 'lucide' set correctly the FIRST time (cannot change later); lucide-react icons only (no CDN, no emojis anywhere); logo URL https://kiro.dev/images/community/events/thumbnails/meetup2.svg. PAYMENT IS FULLY MOCKED: no gateway, no payment-method selection; a Pay / Cancel Payment card; on Pay the order is created with status 'paid' and the UI shows EXACTLY 'The product has been purchased successfully and will be delivered soon'. Currency is INR (₹) everywhere; store money as integer paise in the *_cents columns and format as ₹ in the UI.
key_patterns: Elysia route modules grouped by domain (auth, books, cart, addresses, orders, recommendations) composed under a parent Elysia app with prefix '/api'. Elysia `t` schema validation on every body/query; consistent JSON error shape { error: string } with correct status (401 missing/invalid auth, 400 validation, 403/409 expired cancel window, 404 not found/not owned). A single derive/guard reads the Bearer JWT, verifies it, loads the user id, and makes it available to protected routes; unauthenticated access to protected routes returns 401. DB access via a thin typed query layer in src/db (prepared statements). Frontend: a typed fetch API client in src/frontend/lib/api.ts attaches the stored JWT; an auth context/provider holds the token (persisted in localStorage for convenience ONLY — the server never trusts it for authorization); pages under src/frontend/pages; shadcn primitives under src/frontend/components/ui. Overlays use shadcn Dialog/DropdownMenu/Sonner with conditional rendering so nothing intercepts clicks when closed; the top nav is sticky.
